title: Cryptool vs Hedgey
content_html:
Cryptool vs Hedgey: If you only need on-chain token vesting, Hedgey is the simpler choice. If you need vesting as part of a broader fund or syndicate workflow (including portfolio tracking, investor management, capital raising, and OTC trading) Cryptool.io is the more comprehensive solution.

What Hedgey is good at

Hedgey builds on-chain vesting and lockup infrastructure. Their product focuses on creating, managing and executing token vesting schedules for teams, investors and communities. The contracts handle cliff periods, linear or custom release curves, and claim flows that settlers can trigger without manual intervention. Because the logic lives on-chain, distributions are transparent and auditable by default. Teams that need a dedicated vesting layer (and already have separate tooling for portfolio tracking, investor communications and compliance) often plug Hedgey into that stack.

What Cryptool.io does differently

Cryptool.io (Cryptool) is a Crypto Investment Operating System. Vesting schedules are a native module, but they sit alongside portfolio aggregation across all chains and wallets, fund administration with investor CRM, capital raising with identity verification, an OTC marketplace for allocation trading, syndicate management with per-member tiers, automated investor reporting, and a shared calendar for vesting unlocks and deal events. The vesting module reads the same wallet connections that feed the portfolio view, so allocations, unlocks and investor positions stay in sync without a separate integration layer.

Which one should you pick

Pick Hedgey if your only requirement is a vesting contract layer that you can embed in an existing stack. The product does that one thing well and the on-chain design gives you auditability without extra work.

Pick Cryptool.io if you run a fund, syndicate or launchpad and need vesting inside a system that also tracks positions across every wallet, manages investor relationships, runs raises, produces LP reports, handles OTC trades and keeps a shared calendar of unlocks and deal milestones. The vesting module draws from the same data as the portfolio and reporting modules, so you do not reconcile spreadsheets between tools.

Pick both only if you have a specific reason to keep vesting contracts separate from your fund operations: for example, a regulatory requirement that vesting logic lives in an audited contract suite you control directly. Most teams do not need that separation.

FAQ

What is the main difference in Cryptool vs Hedgey?

Hedgey is a dedicated on-chain vesting protocol. Cryptool.io is an investment operating system that includes vesting alongside portfolio tracking, fund administration, investor reporting, capital raising, OTC trading and syndicate management.

Does Hedgey offer portfolio tracking?

No. Portfolio tracking is not a focus of Hedgey. Cryptool.io tracks balances and positions across all connected wallets and chains automatically.

Can Cryptool.io handle the same vesting schedules as Hedgey?

Yes. Cryptool.io supports cliff periods, linear unlocks and custom release curves with automated distribution to participant wallets. The schedules are configured in the Raise module and execute on-chain.

Is Hedgey non-custodial?

Yes. Hedgey's contracts hold tokens during vesting and release them to beneficiaries. Cryptool.io is also non-custodial: wallet connections are read-only and users sign every transaction.

Which product is better for a crypto fund manager?

Cryptool.io. Fund managers need portfolio aggregation, investor CRM, LP reporting, capital raising and OTC tools in addition to vesting. Cryptool.io includes all of those. Hedgey covers vesting only.

Where can I see Cryptool.io's vesting features in action?

The Raise module walkthrough covers vesting configuration and distribution: https://cryptool.io/blog/cryptool-vs-safelaunch. The syndicate guide shows per-member allocations and unlocks: https://cryptool.io/blog/cryptool-vs-spring.
